banff.overview: Elk and bighorn sheep are frequently seen year-round grazing in valley bottoms and along the Icefields Parkway. Black bears and grizzly bears are reliably spotted foraging during their active months, while moose are occasionally found in wetland areas and along the Icefields Parkway. Coyotes are common near townsites, but wolves remain highly elusive and are rarely encountered. High-elevation rock piles hold hoary marmots and pikas.

angkor.overview: Irrawaddy dolphins are reliably seen on Mekong River boat tours near Kratie, while long-tailed macaques are common year-round among the Angkor temples. In Mondulkiri's eastern forests, yellow-cheeked crested gibbons are elusive but possible to spot on guided dawn treks. A colony of several hundred Lyle's flying foxes roosts in Siem Reap's Royal Independence Gardens.

months.3: Rising heat makes an early-morning start essential for gibbon treks in Mondulkiri. Irrawaddy dolphins are highly concentrated and reliably seen in deep Mekong pools near Kratie.
months.4: Extreme heat makes midday viewing unrewarding. Dawn is essential for spotting elusive gibbons in the eastern forests. Irrawaddy dolphins remain reliably seen in Kratie's deep river pools before the rains arrive.
months.5: Early monsoon rains make the eastern forests muddier, and elusive gibbons are harder to track. Irrawaddy dolphins are still frequently seen at Kratie, though rising river levels expand their range.
months.7: Peak monsoon flooding expands the Tonle Sap lake into the surrounding forest. Eastern forest trails are muddy, making elusive gibbons very difficult to track. Kratie dolphin sightings are occasional.
months.8: Heavy rains continue across Cambodia. Irrawaddy dolphins are occasionally spotted near Kratie as the Mekong runs high. Forest treks for gibbons in Mondulkiri face severe mud and leeches.
months.9: The late monsoon keeps the Mekong River at its highest, making Irrawaddy dolphins elusive near Kratie. Tonle Sap's flooded forests can be reached by boat, though wildlife is spread over a much larger area.

havana.overview: The critically endangered Cuban crocodile lives only in the Zapata Swamp and on the Isle of Youth, and the Boca de Guamá breeding farm is the easiest place to see one. Coastal cays like Cayo Coco hold flocks of American flamingos. Endemic Cuban hutias are occasionally spotted in eastern forests. The rare Cuban solenodon is virtually impossible to find.

months.1: Dry season provides the most reliable access to the Zapata Swamp's interior trails for endemic lizards and frogs. Flamingos can be seen at Cayo Coco, and West Indian manatees live in the coastal waters of Alejandro de Humboldt National Park.
months.2: Stable dry weather keeps the Zapata Swamp trails and boat routes open. Flamingo viewing remains excellent at the northern cays.
months.3: Dry conditions continue to offer peak access to wetland trails and coastal mangroves. Dry conditions keep the Zapata Swamp accessible before the spring rains arrive.
months.4: The late dry season keeps swamp trails accessible for spotting endemic reptiles. Flamingos remain at Cayo Coco, though rising humidity signals the approaching wet season.
months.5: Green sea turtles begin arriving on the beaches of Guanahacabibes Peninsula to nest. Inland, the first heavy rains start to flood the Zapata Swamp, making deep trail access challenging.
months.6: Sea turtle nesting activity increases along the western beaches, requiring guided night walks for reliable sightings. Heavy rains flood the Zapata Swamp and limit boat access.
months.8: Hurricane season brings heavy rains and high winds, frequently washing out roads to the Zapata Swamp and northern cays. Wildlife viewing is severely restricted, though turtle nesting continues on the western beaches.
months.11: The dry season begins, slowly draining the Zapata Swamp and reopening interior trails for endemic reptile spotting. Coastal weather stabilizes.
months.12: Excellent dry-season conditions return. The Zapata Swamp boat routes and the Boca de Guamá crocodile farm are easy to reach, and flamingos can be seen feeding in the shallow waters of the northern cays.

months.2: Peak humpback whale season in Samana Bay offers excellent sightings of breaching adults and newborn calves on dedicated boat tours. Dry conditions provide excellent visibility for spotting flamingos in the southwest lagoons.
months.5: Increasing spring rains can flood trails in Los Haitises and the southwest, making iguana and crocodile spotting more challenging. Sea turtles are nesting: leatherbacks (March to June) mainly at Jaragua National Park and hawksbills (peaking June to September) mainly at Saona Island.
months.6: Hurricane season begins, bringing heavy afternoon downpours that suppress daytime wildlife activity. Leatherback nesting wraps up and hawksbill nesting builds toward its summer peak at protected beaches such as Jaragua and Saona.
months.7: Hot, humid weather at Lago Enriquillo makes early-morning visits the best option. Hawksbill nesting continues at protected beaches such as Saona Island.
months.12: The dry season returns, offering reliable access to Lago Enriquillo for crocodile and iguana sightings. Caribbean flamingos are frequently seen foraging in the coastal lagoons.

borabora.overview: Blacktip reef sharks, lemon sharks, and stingrays are reliably seen year-round in the shallow lagoons of the Society Islands. In the Tuamotu atolls, massive walls of grey reef sharks patrol the deep passes, while green and hawksbill turtles are frequently seen in the lagoons. Humpback whales visit between July and November. As remote oceanic islands, they have no native land mammals, so the focus is on marine life.

luangprabang.overview: Black crested gibbons are the premier wild encounter in Laos, heard and occasionally spotted on multi-day canopy treks in the Bokeo Nature Reserve. Wild animals are hard to see, so the dependable encounters are at ethical sanctuaries, including rescued Asian elephants in Sayaboury and Asiatic black bears at the Tat Kuang Si rescue center.

months.1: Cool, dry weather provides optimal conditions for multi-day canopy treks in Bokeo Nature Reserve to spot black crested gibbons. Rescued elephants and bears can be visited at the sanctuaries.
months.2: Dry trails make February ideal for gibbon trekking in Bokeo Nature Reserve. Asian elephants at Sayaboury sanctuaries and Asiatic black bears at Kuang Si can be visited in comfortable, cool conditions.
months.3: Temperatures rise sharply, making early starts essential for treks in Bokeo. Rescued elephants at Sayaboury sanctuaries can still be visited.
months.4: Peak heat makes canopy treks in Bokeo Nature Reserve physically demanding. Rescued elephants at Sayaboury sanctuaries can still be visited.
months.9: Rains begin to ease, but Bokeo Nature Reserve trails remain waterlogged, keeping wild gibbon trekking difficult. Rescued elephants at Sayaboury sanctuaries can still be visited.
months.10: As the monsoon ends, trails in Bokeo Nature Reserve begin to dry, improving access for multi-day gibbon treks. Rescued Asiatic black bears and Asian elephants can be visited as the weather cools.
months.11: Clear skies and dry trails mark the return of peak conditions for canopy treks to spot black crested gibbons in Bokeo Nature Reserve. Rescued elephants and bears can be visited at the sanctuaries.
months.12: Cool, dry weather offers the year's best conditions for spotting wild black crested gibbons on Bokeo Nature Reserve canopy treks. Rescued elephants and bears can be visited at the sanctuaries.

months.4: Harbor seal pupping continues at Goat Rock Beach and Jenner, where pups are seen resting on the shoreline. Northbound gray whales continue to pass the Sonoma coast, visible from Bodega Head.

belfast-giants-causeway.overview: Grey and harbor seals haul out along the Causeway Coast and Strangford Lough. Inland, elusive red squirrels inhabit the western Fermanagh woodlands, while the native Irish hare is frequently spotted across upland pastures and the Mourne Mountains. Coastal waters occasionally yield harbor porpoise sightings from cliffside vantage points.

months.1: Thousands of pale-bellied brent geese and waders feed across the tidal mudflats of Strangford Lough in autumn and early winter. Grey and harbor seals remain active along the Causeway Coast.
months.2: Strangford Lough's tidal mudflats still hold wintering waders and some brent geese. Coastal seal watching remains reliable, though rough winter seas can limit offshore visibility for porpoises.
months.6: Atlantic puffins and thousands of other breeding seabirds crowd the Rathlin Island cliffs. Summer brings calmer seas to the Causeway Coast, improving the odds of spotting harbor porpoises offshore.
months.9: Grey seals begin their autumn pupping season on secluded beaches and rocky coves.
months.10: Grey seal pupping continues along the coast. Meanwhile, the first large flocks of wintering brent geese arrive at the tidal mudflats of Strangford Lough.
months.11: Thousands of pale-bellied brent geese feed on the Strangford Lough mudflats. Grey seal pups begin weaning and entering the water along the northern rocky coastlines.
months.12: Strangford Lough is an important wintering site for waterfowl, with brent geese and waders on the mudflats. Grey and harbor seals continue to haul out along the Causeway Coast.

tanzania.overview: Over two million wildebeest and plains zebra drive the Great Migration across the Serengeti ecosystem, seen alongside high densities of lions, spotted hyenas, and cheetahs. In the Ngorongoro Crater, elusive black rhinos are occasionally spotted on the open floor, while massive elephant herds congregate around Tarangire National Park's river systems. Forested areas like Arusha National Park support frequently seen black-and-white colobus monkeys. Flamingos gather at soda lakes like Manyara, though numbers fluctuate with water levels.

months.6: The dry season begins, and the Great Migration reaches the western Serengeti, where dramatic Grumeti River crossings occur. In Tarangire National Park, elephant herds begin gathering around the shrinking river.
months.7: Wildebeest and zebra herds arrive in the northern Serengeti, triggering the first spectacular Mara River crossings. Crocodiles are frequently seen ambushing the herds, while Tarangire's elephant concentrations grow.
months.8: Peak dry season forces wildlife to permanent water sources. Mara River crossings in the northern Serengeti are at their most intense, while Tarangire National Park holds hundreds of elephants digging in the dry riverbed.
months.10: The late dry season leaves the landscape parched. Wildebeest herds begin their southward journey from the Mara River, while Tarangire's elephant and buffalo concentrations remain high around the remaining water.
months.11: Short rains typically arrive, triggering fresh grass growth in the eastern and central Serengeti. The wildebeest and zebra herds move rapidly south, while predators follow the shifting herds.

joshua-tree.overview: Peninsular bighorn sheep, an endangered desert race, are occasionally spotted on the rocky slopes around Palm Springs, while coyotes, black-tailed jackrabbits, and roadrunners are frequently seen across the Mojave and Colorado deserts. The region supports specialized arid-adapted reptiles, including the elusive desert tortoise and the large, crevice-dwelling chuckwalla.

quebec-city.overview: Resident St. Lawrence belugas and seasonal migratory whales are the main draw at the Saguenay confluence near Tadoussac, seen from summer boat tours. Inland, moose and beavers are frequently seen in the boreal forests and waterways of Jacques-Cartier National Park, while white-tailed deer are common year-round in Montreal's Mount Royal and surrounding wetlands.

months.4: Tens of thousands of migrating snow geese begin arriving at the Cap Tourmente National Wildlife Area wetlands, creating a massive spectacle.
months.6: Summer boat tours at Tadoussac encounter resident belugas, alongside increasing numbers of migratory minke and fin whales feeding in the St. Lawrence.
months.7: Peak whale watching at Tadoussac offers excellent sightings of belugas and minke whales from boat tours, with blue whales occasionally spotted. Inland, beavers are active at dusk.
months.8: Peak whale watching at Tadoussac offers excellent sightings of belugas and minke whales from boat tours, with blue whales occasionally spotted. Inland, beavers are active at dusk.
months.9: Migratory whales remain on view from Tadoussac boat tours. In Jacques-Cartier National Park, moose enter their autumn rut and are frequently seen foraging near waterways.

whistler.overview: Black bears are frequently seen foraging along the forest edges and ski slopes of Whistler from spring through fall. In the alpine zones of Garibaldi Provincial Park, hoary marmots and pikas are spotted among the talus slopes once the snow clears. Along the coast in Howe Sound and the Strait of Georgia, harbor seals are common year-round, while coastal black-tailed deer frequently browse the lower elevation rainforests and parks.

months.6: Black bears are highly active and frequently spotted along the tree lines and clearings of Whistler. Harbor seals and sea lions can be seen on Howe Sound boat tours, though high alpine trails are still melting.

snowdonia.overview: Red kites gather at the daily feeding at Gigrin Farm near Rhayader and soar across mid-Wales year-round. In Cardigan Bay, a resident population of bottlenose dolphins is frequently spotted on boat tours. Eurasian otters inhabit coastal estuaries and rivers but remain highly elusive.

months.1: Red kites are active year-round in mid-Wales, but coastal wildlife viewing is minimal. Grey seals can occasionally be spotted offshore, though winter storms frequently cancel boat tours.
months.2: Red kites gather at the daily feeding near Rhayader. Coastal wildlife viewing remains limited, with rough winter seas keeping boat tours grounded and marine sightings to a minimum.
months.3: Red kites gather at the daily feeding near Rhayader. Coastal wildlife viewing begins to improve as spring approaches, with occasional bottlenose dolphin sightings in Cardigan Bay on calm days.
months.11: Grey seal pups are still reliably seen on Pembrokeshire beaches early in the month before weaning and heading to sea. Inland, red kites remain a constant presence in mid-Wales.
months.12: Red kites are seen year-round in mid-Wales. Coastal wildlife viewing is minimal, with grey seals dispersed and winter storms frequently canceling Cardigan Bay boat tours.
